models.summary: A Lotka-Volterra web joined to a generalized logistic and a spatial diffusion term, set on the US Corn Belt flattened to a rectangle. Five trophic levels: wheat and weeds, aphids and field mice, ladybugs and bats, eagles and owls, and earthworms, fungi and bacteria. Each chemical (herbicide, insecticide, fertilizer) diffuses, is applied during one phase of the cycle, and decays. The producer equation adds the logistic limit, predation, weed suppression, and a wheat boost. Carrying capacity is a baseline plus decomposer and fertilizer gains minus herbicide and insecticide losses. Consumers are supported by the level below with a saturation constant and lose to the level above, to insecticide, and to mortality. The decomposer draws on the deaths of all four levels and is inhibited by all three chemicals. A two-harmonic seasonal function multiplies growth. The system is solved by finite volume on a 6 by 6 grid. Without insecticide the pests consume the producers and the web collapses.

models.summary: A return layer built on the FATE web. A species distribution model gives the probability that bees, larks, and shrubs come back, from habitat maturity, climate, chemical intensity, agricultural intensity, and time; all three score above 0.78. Three pairwise reintroductions at month 24: bees with shrubs (weakest, shrubs compete with the crop), larks with bees (fast growth, early fluctuation), larks with shrubs (best). Herbicide use is full until month 24, declines linearly over 36 months, and stops at month 60. Bats enter as a pollination gain on crop productivity; frogs enter as a capacity gain and get their own diffusion equation. A resilience index weights each species' deviation from its equilibrium by a time decay, and bats score 6.42 against 5.01 for frogs.

models.summary: A two-objective program over three decisions: organic fertilizer, biological control, and buffer area. The ecological objective integrates biodiversity and stability minus a weighted pest density. The economic objective integrates wheat yield times market price minus cost. Four constraints: species totals above a floor, soil nutrients within a tolerance, herbicide use under a decaying cap, and spending under a budget. The model is declared concave, so strong duality holds, and it is solved by a Lagrangian dual with the epsilon-constraint method. The combined objective weights ecology at lambda. The run gives 243.58 for ecology, 13484.36 USD per month for income, weights 0.36, 0.29 and 0.45, and lambda of 0.57, so ecology wins the trade.
